messages:
maria (support): heads-up — enterprise customer 'BigBank' just opened a P1. They say requests that should be EU-only are showing US region IDs in our response headers. They flagged this as a data residency breach and want timeline + repro. ticket: INC-3241

raj (oncall): ack. can you paste the response headers they sent and the customer account id?

maria (support): pasted their snippet below (redacted):

```
X-Redwood-Region: us-east-1
X-Request-ID: rwd_8a3f7c
Account-ID: acct-9891-eu
```

They say they always send region_hint=eu-west-1 in the request. Customer says this started after an incident around 09:10 UTC where they saw 502s.

raj (oncall): thanks. adding oliver (sre) and bringing up our audit logs now. @sre-bot can you surface any cross-region failover events for acct-9891-eu between 09:00-09:30 UTC?

sre-bot: policy_exceptions:1, failover_events:3 for acct-9891-eu in window 09:04-09:22 UTC. Automatic fallback executed due to capacity pressure in eu-west-1 at 09:04:12 UTC. All fallback calls routed to us-east-1 to maintain availability. Exception code: Fallback:CapacitySpike. Audit log IDs: audit-7721,audit-7722,audit-7723.

oliver (sre): confirmed. our routing policy allowed cross-region fallback for this plan tier. The autopolicy kicked in when EU pool hit safety threshold (spike from 4->13 req/s sustained). That triggered a fallback to us-east to keep latency SLA.

maria (support): customer insists this violates their contract for EU-only processing. They want exact list of requests that were routed and timestamps.

oliver (sre): pulling request-level audit entries now. quick note: the account's account-level setting 'residency_enforcement' is currently set to "soft" (fallthrough allowed). If it were "strict", fallback would have been blocked and requests would have failed instead of being routed.

emily (legal): we need the list and a timeline. if data left the EU, this is a policy exception and we must escalate. Also need the decision rationale and who approved the fallback policy for this customer.

oliver (sre): copying sanitized audit lines for the affected calls:

```
audit-7721 | 2026-01-18T09:04:12Z | acct-9891-eu | req rwd_8a3f7c | routed_from=eu-west-1 -> us-east-1 | reason=CapacitySpike | fallback_policy=soft
audit-7722 | 2026-01-18T09:05:47Z | acct-9891-eu | req rwd_8a4b12 | routed_from=eu-west-1 -> us-east-1 | reason=CapacitySpike | fallback_policy=soft
```

oliver (sre): repro steps for us to reproduce locally:
1) set test account residency_enforcement=soft
2) flood eu-west-1 trial pool with sustained requests to exceed safety_threshold (we used: for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -H "region_hint: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate ; done)
3) watch routing decision logs: /internal/routing/decisions?account=acct-9891-eu

raj (oncall): temporary mitigation: set residency_enforcement=strict for acct-9891-eu to block cross-region routing, then repro to confirm requests fail instead of leaving region. Also propose immediate capacity bump for EU pool for this account under Dedicated plan or move them to reserved capacity.

aj (sales): flagged to the CSM. BigBank is on an enterprise contract — they're furious. we need a short blameless summary and proposed remediation for the account.

emily (legal): also need to confirm whether any PII was present in payloads for those routed calls. If so, prepare incident notification template.

maria (support): I told the customer we would: 1) provide timeline & audit IDs, 2) offer to pin region or flip strict enforcement, 3) discuss procurement of Dedicated capacity or a backup EU capacity reservation, and 4) share internal remediation plan. they're waiting for ETA.

oliver (sre): ETA for initial timeline & audit IDs: 30 min. ETA for root cause + remediation plan: 4 hours (we need capacity metrics, routing histograms, and decision logs re: safety threshold tuning).

raj (oncall): quick workaround command to pin the account to EU-only (applies immediately):
```
# PATCH /internal/accounts/:account_id/settings
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"residency_enforcement":"strict"}' \
  https://internal-admin.redwood.ai/accounts/acct-9891-eu/settings
```

maria (support): executed with ops' help. changed to strict at 09:28 UTC and confirmed subsequent customer calls returned X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1. passing note to customer.

aj (sales): please include a credit proposal for the impacted window in the remediation note.

emily (legal): keep IOC (indicators of compromise) notes if we find payload-level PII. Also preserve all logs for 90 days per compliance request.

oliver (sre): logging this as INC-3241 in our incident tracker. I'll attach raw audit exports (s3://internal-incidents/INC-3241/audit-export-1769564321.csv) and include routing decision snapshots.

maria (support): customer responded: they accept strict enforcement for now but want written confirmation + a follow-up call with engineering & legal. scheduling.

raj (oncall): will run postmortem checklist after remediation. main action items: (A) review fallback_policy defaults for enterprise EU accounts, (B) add stronger preflight alerts when fallback would cause cross-region residency exceptions, (C) consider an opt-in capacity reservation prompt when account shows high traffic patterns.

maria (support): closing loop here for now. will update ticket and attach the audit IDs and the S3 export link. if anything else emerges, re-open thread. :white_check_mark:
